newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude in doldrums, paper weak as futures sli.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude in doldrums, paper weak as futures sli.

text.p: North Sea wet players hung back cautiously on Thursday in the wake of a big slide in outright values but most crude differentials were still notionally assessed around Wednesday's levels, traders said.
Paper was steady to weaker, with May Brent changing hands at $18.32, some 80 cents weaker than Tuesday's values but in line with Wednesday's.
Outright Brent on the screen was also easier. IPE May Brent futures were 14 cents weaker at $18.37 a barrel at 1057 GMT, catching up with a late sell-off in New York.
"It looks ugly. We're still under pressure," a wet crude trader said. "When you get big moves on the screen it tends to hold things up while people try to figure out what the heck is going on."
Attention remained focused on what BP planned to do with up to 12 early April Brents it still holds. Both Brent April 17-19 cargoes in Wednesday's chains were again kept by BP.
No dates were expected from the paper chains on Thursday.
The slide in Dated values has been boosting European refinery margins, with $2.15 a barrel seen on Wednesday for a complex configuration refinery in Rotterdam.
The last time such levels were seen was in November 1996.
CFDs for next week eased around three cents to June -95/-88 cents, with April 14-18 steady at June -75/-70 cents and April 21-25 eight cents weaker at June -68/-60.
The May/June spread softened slightly to -24/-20 cents from Wednesday's traded level of -21 cents.
Weaker Dubai helped widen May Brent/Dubai by up to five cents to $1.75/$1.80, with June at $1.55/$1.60.
May/June Dubai was talked in London at -25/-15 cents, firmer than earlier Singapore spreads of -30/-20. June/July in London was -5/-2 cents, with July/August was assessed at flat to 3 cts.
